articles.text: BÀBA: Èi, Xiǎo Èr xiàle bān, jíjímángmángde yòu dào nǎr qù le?
FATHER: Say, where did Xiǎo Èr go off to in such a rush after work?
MĀMA: Tā shuō, qù gēn tāde yíge tóngxué xué Yīngwén dǎ zì.
MOTHER: He said he was going to learn English typing from a classmate.
BÀBA: Xué Yīngwén dǎ zì? Shi nántóngxué háishi nǚtóngxué?
FATHER: To learn English typing? Was it a male classmate or a female classmate?
MĀMA: Jiù shi shàngcì láiguode nèige nǚtóngxué.
MOTHER: It's the female classmate who was over last time.
BÀBA: Xiǎo Èr yàoshi àishang nèige nǚháizi jiu máfan le.
FATHER: If Xiǎo Èr falls in love with that girl it's going to be trouble.
MĀMA: Yǒu shénme máfan? Nà háizi shi dàxuéshēng, yòu yǒu lǐmào, láile hái bāng wǒ zuò fàn shénmede. Yǒu shénme bù hǎo?
MOTHER: What trouble? That girl is a college student, and well mannered. And when she came over she even helped me cook and so on. What's wrong with that?
BÀBA: Nǐ zhīdao shénme? Tā fùqin yǒu zhèngzhì wèntí.
FATHER: What do you know? Her father has political problems.
MĀMA: Bú duì ba?! Wǒ tīng Xiǎo Èr shuō, jīnnián xiàtian tā rù Tuán le. Yàoshi tā fùqin yǒu zhèngzhì wèntíde huà, tā néng rù Tuán ma?
MOTHER: You must be wrong! I've heard from Xiǎo Èr that she joined the Communist Youth League this summer. If her father had political problems, could she join the League?
BÀBA: Néng, xiànzài yǒu zhèngcè, zhǐ yào háizi hǎo, jiu kěyi rù Tuán, bù guǎn tā fùmǔde wèntí yǒu duō dà.
FATHER: Yes. Now there's a policy that as long as the child is good, he or she can enter the League, no matter how great his or her parents' problems are.
MĀMA: Zhè jiu duì le ma, wǒ shuō nèi háizi shi hǎo háizi!
MOTHER: There you have it, then! I said she was a good child.
BÀBA: Bù xíng, háishi děi ràng tāmen fēnkāi, yǐhòu máfan tài duō!
FATHER: No, it won't do. We should still make them break up. There will be too much trouble later on.
MĀMA: Shéi méiyou máfan? Gāogànde háizi jiu méiyou máfan le?
MOTHER: Who doesn't have trouble? Do you think the children of senior cadres don't have any trouble?
MĀMA: Lín Biāo cóngqián yě shi dà gànbu, nǐ néng ràng nǐ érzi gēn tā nǚér jiéhūn ma?
MOTHER: Lín Biāo was a big cadre too, but would you let your son marry his daughter?
BÀBA: Hǎo hǎo hǎo, bié shuō le. Háizide shì zhēn bù hǎo bàn!
FATHER: Okay, okay. Don't say any more! Children's matters are really hard to handle.
MĀMA: Yǒu shénme bù hǎo bànde?! Zhǐ yào nèi háizi běnrén hǎo, tāmen yòu hùxiāng xǐhuan, jiu xíng le.
MOTHER: What's hard to handle? As long as the girl herself is good, and they like each other, it will be fine.
BÀBA: Hǎo hǎo hǎo! Tīng nǐde.
FATHER: Okay. We'll do as you say.
